issues.legal_issue: A state may levy a cess on coal-bearing and other mineral-bearing land when the levy is in substance a tax on land or mineral rights, even though the measure of the levy reflects the minerals produced.
material_facts: The amended state laws classified land by whether it was coal-bearing, mineral-bearing, or neither, and imposed cess by reference to the land’s assessed value, which was calculated using mineral production.
The challenge asserted that central legislation on mines and mineral development deprived the state legislature of competence to impose the cess.
The central legislation did not impose a limitation on the state’s power to tax land or mineral rights that the state had breached.
issues.conclusion: The amendments imposing cess on coal-bearing and mineral-bearing land were intra vires the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 245, 246 and 248 and Entries 49 and 50 of List II, the State may tax land and mineral rights; Entries 52 and 54 of List I concern control, regulation and development, not taxation as such. The subject of a tax is distinct from its measure, and a tax on land may be measured by its productivity or value. The Court applied the pith-and-substance approach and relied on Goodricke Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal, Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. v. State of Orissa, Ralla Ram v. Province of East Punjab, Anant Mills v. State of Gujarat and other decisions on land taxation. India Cement and Orissa Cement were distinguishable because the levies there were on royalty, not on land; Mahanadi Coalfields was overruled.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess and (levy_directly_related_to_land or levy_on_mineral_rights) and (central_law_does_not_limit_state_taxing_power or levy_measured_by_land_productivity)

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess: A party challenged the constitutionality of a state-imposed cess.
predicates.levy_directly_related_to_land: The levy was imposed on land or had a direct and definite relationship with the land.
predicates.levy_on_mineral_rights: The levy was imposed on rights associated with minerals in the land.
predicates.central_law_does_not_limit_state_taxing_: The central legislation did not impose a limitation on the state’s power to tax land or mineral rights that the state exceeded.
predicates.levy_measured_by_land_productivity: The levy was quantified by reference to the land’s productivity or its mineral output.

issues.definition: When a party challenges a state cess and the levy is on land or mineral rights, or is measured by land productivity, and no applicable central limitation is exceeded, the cess is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: A cess on tea-estate land remains a tax on land when its amount is measured by the tea leaves produced there.
material_facts: The state law imposed cess annually on tea estates, defined to include land used for growing tea and associated land and buildings.
The amount of cess was determined by the quantity of green tea leaves produced on the estate.
The challenge relied on central control of the tea industry and argued that the levy was actually on tea production rather than land.
issues.conclusion: The cess on tea estates was intra vires the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 49 of List II permits taxation of land, including land classified by its use; yield or income may be used as the measure without changing the subject of the tax. Central control of an industry under Entry 52 of List I does not itself confer on the Union the power to tax land used by that industry. The Court affirmed Goodricke Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal, relying on the distinction between the subject and measure of a tax and on the principles in Ralla Ram, D.G. Gouse & Co. v. State of Kerala and related cases.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess: A party challenged the constitutionality of a state-imposed cess.
predicates.tea_estate_land_is_subject_of_levy: The levy was imposed on land used as a tea estate.
predicates.tea_yield_is_only_measure_of_levy: The quantity of tea produced was used to calculate the levy rather than being its legal subject.

issues.definition: If a challenged cess is imposed on tea-estate land and tea yield is only its measure, the cess on that land is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: A cess measured by the quantity of brick earth removed from land may be imposed as a tax on land or mineral rights, including when the earth is consumed captively in brick manufacture.
material_facts: The challenged state laws imposed cess on mineral-bearing land or quarry by reference to quantities of materials dispatched.
Brick earth was extracted and used to manufacture bricks at the brickfield or nearby, and the owners argued that no dispatch occurred because the earth was consumed on site.
Brick earth was a minor mineral, but the challenged levy was not a levy on royalty.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the cess on brick earth was dismissed; the levy was constitutionally valid, and removal for captive use could be treated as dispatch for the purpose of the levy.
issues.legal_principle: Entries 49 and 50 of List II permit a tax on land or mineral rights, and the quantity removed may serve as a measure of the levy. The meaning of dispatch in this setting includes removal of material to a place of captive consumption, even within the same complex; the levy does not become a tax on the manufactured product merely because it is calculated by reference to the material used. The Court applied its reasoning on land taxation in Goodricke Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal and distinguished India Cement and Orissa Cement.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess and brick_earth_is_removed_from_land and (brick_earth_is_used_captively or brick_earth_is_sent_elsewhere)

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess: A party challenged the constitutionality of a state-imposed cess.
predicates.brick_earth_is_removed_from_land: Brick earth was taken from land or a quarry.
predicates.brick_earth_is_used_captively: The removed brick earth was consumed in brick manufacture at the same site or nearby.
predicates.brick_earth_is_sent_elsewhere: The removed brick earth was transported to another place.

issues.definition: If a challenged cess is measured by brick earth removed from land, whether for captive use or transport elsewhere, the cess is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: A local development authority may impose a cess on mineral rights to fund development and services in its special area when the levy does not intrude on central regulation of mines and minerals.
material_facts: A state law established a special area development authority with powers and duties to plan and develop its area and to provide municipal services and infrastructure.
The authority imposed a cess on mineral rights, and the proceeds were directed to a fund for administering the law.
Mining activity in the area involved extraction and transport of minerals and affected local infrastructure and the environment.
The challenge argued that central mineral legislation occupied the field and that the cess effectively increased royalty.
issues.conclusion: The cess was constitutionally valid, whether treated as a tax or a fee, and the decision upholding it was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Entries 5, 49, 50 and 66 of List II support local governance, taxation of land and mineral rights, and fees for matters within the State List. Entry 54 of List I and the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 do not, without a specific limitation or charging provision, reserve taxation of mineral rights to the Union. A fee may be supported by a general nexus between those bearing it and the services funded; it need not correspond directly to each payer’s benefit. The Court relied on Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. v. State of Orissa, Western Coalfields Ltd. v. Special Area Development Authority and Goodricke Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal.

rule.if: challenge_to_local_development_cess and authority_has_local_development_duties and cess_funds_area_development_or_services and central_law_does_not_limit_state_taxing_power

predicates.challenge_to_local_development_cess: A party challenged a cess imposed by a local development authority.
predicates.authority_has_local_development_duties: The authority was responsible for planned development or municipal functions in its area.
predicates.cess_funds_area_development_or_services: The cess proceeds funded administration, development, infrastructure, or services for the area.
predicates.central_law_does_not_limit_state_taxing_: The central legislation did not impose a limitation on the state’s power to tax mineral rights that the state exceeded.

issues.definition: If a challenged local cess funds an authority’s development or service duties and does not exceed a central limitation on state taxing power, it is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: Royalty paid for the right to extract minerals is not a tax, and a decision stating otherwise because of an apparent drafting error does not establish that royalty is a tax.
material_facts: The Court considered the wording in a prior judgment that appeared to state that royalty was a tax, despite that judgment also describing royalty as payment for use of land.
The Court reviewed the established understanding of royalty as payment to the owner for minerals extracted or the privilege of extracting them.
The cess at issue in the earlier case was imposed on royalty, rather than directly on land.
issues.conclusion: Royalty is not a tax, and the earlier judgment did not decide that royalty itself was a tax.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated royalty as consideration or a return associated with a mining lease, distinct from a tax imposed by sovereign authority. It corrected the apparent omission of the words “cess on” in the relevant sentence of India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu, explaining that the judgment’s intended statement concerned cess on royalty. It relied on D.K. Trivedi & Sons v. State of Gujarat, H.R.S. Murthy v. Collector of Chittoor, and the distinction between royalty and tax in other authorities.

predicates.constitutional_interpretation_of_prior_t: The Court was interpreting the legal effect of a prior judgment on a tax issue.
predicates.prior_judgment_has_apparent_textual_erro: The prior judgment contained wording inconsistent with its reasoning and the surrounding text.
predicates.royalty_is_payment_for_mineral_extractio: The payment was made as consideration for the right to extract or use minerals.

issues.definition: When a prior tax judgment contains an apparent textual error and the payment is consideration for mineral extraction rights, royalty is not a tax.

issues.legal_issue: A state cess imposed on royalty is not a tax on land merely because royalty is calculated by reference to minerals extracted from land.
material_facts: The earlier levy was calculated as an additional charge on royalty payable under a mining lease.
The levy’s subject was royalty rather than land itself, and royalty was treated as payment for mineral extraction rights.
The challenge concerned the state legislature’s competence to impose that additional charge.
issues.conclusion: The earlier levy on royalty was outside the state legislature’s competence and could not be sustained as a tax on land.
issues.legal_principle: A tax on land under Entry 49 of List II must be directly imposed on land and bear a definite relationship to it. A cess imposed on royalty is an additional charge on the payment for mineral extraction rights, not a tax directly on land; royalty is not itself a tax. The Court clarified India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu and distinguished that case from levies genuinely imposed on land, as in Goodricke Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_cess: A party challenged the constitutionality of a state-imposed cess.
predicates.cess_is_imposed_on_royalty: The cess was calculated as an additional charge on royalty payable for mineral extraction.
predicates.levy_is_not_directly_imposed_on_land: The legal subject of the levy was not land itself.

issues.definition: If a challenged cess is imposed on royalty and not directly on land, it cannot be upheld as a tax on land.

issues.legal_issue: A validating law that gives constitutional force to previously invalidated state mineral cess provisions permits enforcement of the liabilities those provisions created, not merely retention of sums already collected.
material_facts: A central validating law incorporated the relevant provisions of state laws imposing cess or taxes on minerals.
The dispute concerned whether states could collect validated cess liabilities that had accrued but remained unpaid, or only retain amounts already collected.
A later decision had limited the validating law to preserving amounts already collected.
issues.conclusion: The validating law authorized enforcement of validated liabilities as well as retention of sums already collected; P. Kannadasan was correctly decided, and District Mining Officer v. Tata Iron and Steel Co. did not state the correct law.
issues.legal_principle: The effect of a validating enactment must be determined from its language and the rights and obligations it creates. Where the enactment validates the underlying state provisions without distinguishing collected sums from outstanding liabilities, the validated liabilities may be enforced. The Court relied on the Cess and Other Taxes on Minerals (Validation) Act, 1992, P. Kannadasan v. State of Tamil Nadu and District Mining Officer v. Tata Iron and Steel Co., rejecting the latter decision’s restriction of the validating law’s effect.

predicates.dispute_about_validated_mineral_cess_lia: A dispute concerned enforcement of a liability under state mineral cess provisions covered by a validating law.
predicates.validating_law_validates_underlying_cess: The validating law gave legal effect to the underlying state provisions that imposed the cess.
predicates.validating_law_does_not_limit_effect_to_: The validating law did not restrict its effect to amounts already collected.

issues.definition: If a validating law gives effect to the underlying cess provisions and does not limit that effect to collected sums, outstanding validated liabilities may be enforced.
